name: Google One
tagline: Back up selected personal files and photos to a user-owned storage target

pricing.notes: Official US monthly price for 2 TB; regional pricing differs.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 15 GB shared across Drive, Gmail and Photos
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual on public 100 GB, 2 TB and 5 TB plans (save up to 16%); some high-capacity upgrade-only plans are monthly only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Google does not sell metered storage overage: when the account is full, new Drive uploads, Photos backups and some Gmail functions stop until storage is freed or the plan is upgraded. Extra capacities and AI bundles vary by account and region.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Google One, back up selected personal files and photos to a user-owned storage target. The hard boundary is google account integration, photos, device backup, family sharing, and global infrastructure, plus reliability, durability, and cross-device sync.
coreLoopDIY: Back up selected personal folders and photos, encrypt files client-side, track versions, and restore them from user-owned object storage.
whatYouLose: Google account integration, Photos, device backup, family sharing, and global infrastructure
ongoingBurden: chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Google One because storage subscriptions sell confidence that files will still exist after a lost device, bad sync, or provider incident. The recurring cost buys chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Nextcloud
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source file sync and collaboration server.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Files
alternatives.desc: File sync plus phone photo uploads on storage you own; Google’s invisible operations team is gone.

facts.install: Deploy Nextcloud All-in-One with Docker, or perform a manual web-server, PHP and database installation
facts.dataFormat: Files live in the configured local data directory or object storage; metadata, shares, versions and application state live in a supported SQL database
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not replace pooled Gmail, Drive and Photos storage, Android device backup or Google Photos' search and editing intelligence.
facts.setupBlocker: A server plus Docker or a full web stack, DNS and TLS, and a plan for upgrades, backups and storage failures

alternatives.name: OpenCloud
alternatives.desc: Files and automatic photo uploads across desktop and mobile, provided you run the cloud yourself.

facts.install: Use the documented Docker Compose and Traefik stack; a single-binary deployment is also possible
facts.dataFormat: The base deployment stores file data and metadata in its configured POSIX instance directory; an optional decomposed backend stores blobs in S3 and metadata on POSIX storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It provides files and photo upload, but none of Google One's Gmail, Google Photos or device-backup ecosystem integration.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, a domain and open ports, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration, and operational responsibility for the storage directory

alternatives.name: Seafile Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Desktop file sync and automatic mobile photo backup, with a database and server attached.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: File libraries are stored as deduplicated blocks with Git-like repository, commit and filesystem objects rather than ordinary folders, while metadata lives in relational databases
facts.gapVsPaid: It syncs files and camera uploads but does not provide Google Photos intelligence or full Google-service and device backups.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, MariaDB, Caddy or another proxy, a domain and TLS, plus coordinated backups of both databases and block storage

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium 2 TB plan and a single-user encrypted backup DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Google One in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, MinIO, and a Tauri 2 sync client; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: back up selected personal folders and photos, encrypt files client-side, track versions, and restore them from user-owned object storage.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a desktop client that watches explicitly selected folders and ignores configured patterns.
Chunk, hash, compress, and encrypt files locally before uploading to the configured object store.
Store version metadata, tombstones, device identifiers, and integrity checks in PostgreSQL.
Provide upload and restore queues with pause, retry, bandwidth limits, and resumable transfers.
Add file history, point-in-time restore, key export, storage usage, and scheduled restore tests.
Document the failure model and make clear that one server is not a complete backup strategy.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out multi-provider consumer sync at global scale.
Deliberately leave out guaranteed durability or ransomware recovery.
Deliberately leave out shared-drive administration, mobile apps, and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
